leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer B016 as a single-part prize built on the physiology and active form of GLP-1, with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov as laureates. They share the view that the discovery chain from proglucagon processing and GLP-1(7-36) to incretin therapies is mature and clinically very large. They are not fully aligned on how firmly to rest on Mojsov: several state that her priority against Habener (not on the credited list) is contested and that the Knudsen configuration would be the fallback if it cannot be resolved.

Two members prefer B016 as a single-part prize with Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, carrying the physiology through to the long-acting analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide). They share the view that the arc from discovery to medicine is the point of the prize and that Knudsen's engineering step made the biology matter to patients. They differ from the first group only in the third laureate and in the citation wording (development into long-acting therapies versus the active peptide). Both acknowledge that the basic-discovery trio is defensible.

areas_of_agreement: All six members ranked B016 first in the opening round and all six place B016 in their preferred configuration, as the only ballot in every configuration.
All six members describe B016 as scientifically original, mechanistically clear, independently confirmed and clinically very large, with no maturity concern.
All six members include Drucker and Holst in their preferred laureate set.
All six members name B007 (CAR-T) as an alternative, and none of them proposes more than one prize part in the preferred configuration.
All six members state that no specific conflict applies to the shortlisted ballots.
scientific_disputes: Whether the prize should be framed around hormone physiology and the identification of the active peptide, or around the physiology and its development into long-acting drugs; this decides the citation wording.

Whether a method or tool prize such as optogenetics (B008) or massively parallel sequencing (B003) fits the discovery criterion as well as a disease-oriented discovery. One member ranks B003 second, while another ranks it outside the top group.

Whether mechanism alone is enough for a prize when clinical benefit is still prospective, as in cGAS-STING (B005) and the unfolded protein response (B043), compared with ballots that already have outcome evidence.
Whether Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer is a distinct lineage from engineered chimeric receptors in CAR-T (B007), which affects whether June and Sadelain alone are a clean pair.
attribution_disputes: For B016, the third laureate: four members choose Mojsov and two choose Knudsen. Every member notes that the three-person limit leaves out either the identification of the active peptide or the long-acting analogues.
Mojsov's priority for identifying and synthesising active GLP-1 is described as contested by the Habener group, who are not on the credited list, and the supplied record does not resolve it.
For B007, members note that Eshhar is absent from the credited names and ask how Rosenberg, June and Sadelain should be treated.
For B008, six credited names cannot be cut to three without a disputed choice, and the prize history of method awards gives no clean guide.
For B005, the allocation among Chen, Barber and Ishikawa within five credited names remains open.
maturity_disputes: No member raises a maturity concern for B016.
The clinical translation of optogenetics (B008), such as vision restoration, is described as early.
STING-targeted therapeutics (B005) are described as unproven, and the clinical consequence of the unfolded protein response (B043) as largely prospective.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member declares a recusal-level conflict for any shortlisted ballot.

El-Manira notes that his neuroscience field overlaps with optogenetics (B008) as a user community, and the chair notes in the process record that this ballot is close to his own field; neither is a documented tie to a credited name.

Sandberg notes that his single-cell methods rely on massively parallel sequencing (B003), and Linnarsson notes that his spatial transcriptomics work and co-authorship with Sandberg are adjacent to B003; neither involves a ballot in their preferred configuration.
Wahren-Herlenius notes topical overlap with cGAS-STING (B005) and with CAR-T use in autoimmunity (B007), without a documented personal or institutional tie.

Perlmann notes his Ludwig Institute affiliation, with no documented involvement in the cancer-therapy candidates, and the chair notes about twenty co-authored works with Perlmann and a postdoctoral period with Greengard, who is not a candidate.
questions_for_round2: For B016, can the committee defend Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide against the Habener claim on the supplied record? If not, should Knudsen take the third place?
Should the B016 citation recognise physiology and the active peptide only, or the full arc through long-acting analogues, and which laureate set follows from that choice?
Should B016 stand alone as a single prize part, or should it be reduced to one or two names so that a second part such as B007 can be added? If so, which names should be dropped?
If B007 is added, can June and Sadelain be recognised without Rosenberg and Eshhar, and can the committee defend that exclusion?
Is there a principled basis for ranking a tool or method ballot (B008, B003) against disease-oriented discovery, and if so how should the six optogenetics names be reduced to three?
Is a mechanism-only discovery (B005, B043) sufficient for a prize this year, or should those ballots wait for clinical evidence?
summary.chair_observation: The six round-1 files agree on B016 as the leading ballot and split four to two only on the third laureate, Mojsov or Knudsen. Every member names attribution, not scientific importance or maturity, as the main reservation. Alternatives are scattered after B007, and no member has yet made a full case for a second prize part, so round 2 should resolve the B016 laureate set and whether a second part is wanted.
